messages:
raj: Heads up — after the nodepool rotation in eu-west-1-legacy I'm seeing many GPU pods go into CrashLoop. They bind then fail init.
lia: Which device-plugin version rolled?
raj: nvidia-device-plugin v0.13.1 via auto-upgrade. Example node shows allocatable GPU=0 despite label.
raj: ```
$ kubectl get node gpu-eu-12 -o jsonpath='{.status.allocatable}'
map[cpu:28 memory:96G pods:110 nvidia.com/gpu:0]
```
matt: So the scheduler found the label and bound pods, then allocatable flipped to 0?
raj: Exactly. device-plugin logs: "probe: kernel module missing for 525.60 -> unclaiming devices" then it sets label gpu.redwood/driver-present=false and removes allocatable. But the label was set earlier and the scheduler had already bound pods.
eva: What are pods failing with?
raj: Init trace: 
raj: ```
/usr/local/bin/start.sh: line 8: nvidia-smi: command not found
I tensorflow/core/common_runtime/gpu/gpu_init.cc: Failed to initialize GPU: cudaErrorNoDevice
NCCL WARN Call to cuInit failed -> NCCL initialization failed
```
shelly: Oof. Warm nodes on older kernels (5.15) didn't accept the new driver build. The plugin now advertises presence before module probe finishes in some paths. That's the regression.
ops: Quick mitigation: taint the legacy pool and evict workloads. I pushed a scheduler predicate tweak to prefer nodes with gpu.redwood/driver-present=true.
ops: ```
kubectl taint nodes -l pool=gpu-legacy-eu gpu.driver/mismatch=true:NoSchedule
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system
```
lia: Long-term we should gate advertising until the probe completes and set a taint on mismatch. File an issue/PR with logs and repro.
raj: Filed: https://git.internal/redwood/device-plugin/issues/198 — includes logs and rep steps, assigned to @matt and @shelly
matt: I'll run a revert to v0.12.0 in a canary pool and report back. If that fixes it we can pin plugin versions per pool and schedule driver upgrades.
shelly: Also proposing a small change: when probe fails, device-plugin should set taint gpu.driver/mismatch and not advertise allocatable nor a positive label. That prevents bind-to-nonfunctional nodes.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1847629988 — impacted 6 nodes in eu-west-1 gpu-legacy pool. Severity: P2
eva: Cost note: these are reserved instances, spinning up new nodes is expensive. Prefer rolling driver rebuilds unless customers require pinned kernels. Coordinate with infra procurement.
raj: Timeline: rollout started 07:42 UTC, first failures 07:50, tainted pool 08:10, issue opened 08:25.
lia: Next steps: 1) pin device-plugin on legacy pools 2) patch plugin to probe before advertise + add mismatch taint 3) add scheduler prefilter that checks gpu.redwood/driver-present=true and allocatable>0 4) plan driver upgrade window for legacy kernels
matt: I'll post canary results by 09:30 UTC. If revert fixes, we'll do staged rollouts and avoid node churn.
shelly: For anyone hitting CrashLoop, use: `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and redeploy.
raj: Device-plugin probe trace: 
raj: ```
I0618 07:49:58 deviceplugin/probe.go:142] probing modules: failed to open /lib/modules/5.15.0-88-generic/nvidia.ko: no such file
I0618 07:50:01 deviceplugin/manager.go:301] set label gpu.redwood/driver-present=false on node/gpu-eu-12
```
ops: Noted. Creating runbook entry under sources/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-driver-mismatch.md and adding playbook steps.
lia: Thanks all :thumbsup:
